summary: Verified hero-banner-loads-late performance fix. Backend GET /api/settings caching works (cold ~552ms → warm ~350ms, sub-second on all calls). Frontend hero renders promptly: hero appears within ~1s of DOMContentLoaded and fully loads at ~2s. Cloudinary transform 'f_auto,q_auto,w_1920' is correctly injected into hero image src. First hero has fetchpriority='high', loading='eager', decoding='sync' as intended. Hero text overlay, welcome-home, customize, worlds, and category bento sections all render. Festive settings JSON still contains valid {title, category_id=18, category_slug='festive-collections', enabled:true}. No functional regressions.

console_warnings.issue: React DOM warning: 'Invalid DOM property `fetchpriority`. Did you mean `fetchPriority`?'. React expects camelCase `fetchPriority` in JSX. Currently the attribute is still applied correctly at the DOM level (verified in DOM), but the console warning appears on every render. Recommend renaming `fetchpriority` prop → `fetchPriority` in Home.jsx line 41.

action_items: MINOR: In /app/frontend/src/pages/Home.jsx line 41, rename JSX prop `fetchpriority` → `fetchPriority` (camelCase) to silence the React console warning. Functionality is unaffected.
critical_code_review_comments: Home.jsx is 617 lines and mixes many sections (Hero, Customize form, Worlds, Bento, ProductSections, OurStory) — consider splitting each section into its own file for maintainability (>700 line threshold approaching).

cloudinaryOptimize() is a simple string replace and does not preserve existing transforms if an admin uploads an image URL that already has /upload/{transform}/... — currently fine because uploads have no pre-transform, but worth guarding.
Hero lacks explicit width/height attributes; adding intrinsic dimensions would further reduce CLS.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Hero perf fix verified end-to-end. Backend cache (festive_cat_id, 300s TTL) is working — /api/settings warms to ~350ms after first call. Frontend hero uses Cloudinary f_auto,q_auto,w_1920 transform. Only remaining nit is React JSX prop casing (`fetchpriority` → `fetchPriority`).
